title: Loss of Seat Power and Screen Blanking in the Upper Deck Premium Cabin
abstract: Emerald Coast Air reports repeated in-flight loss of seat power and screen blanking in the upper deck premium cabin, concentrated on long sectors, and asks for a design answer rather than the present reset procedure.

sections.request: On our long sectors the cabin crew are resetting the entertainment system in the upper deck front cabin two or three times a flight. What the passengers see is the screen going black and the laptop socket at the seat dying at the same time, usually an hour or two after the meal service when everybody is charging something. The crew reset brings it back for a while and then it goes again. We have replaced the boxes under the seats, we have replaced whole seat groups, and the fault follows the cabin rather than the hardware. Our premium passengers are the ones affected, which is the part that hurts. We would like Aeralis to look at whether the cabin was ever designed for the load that modern devices actually draw, and to give us a permanent answer rather than a reset card.
sections.background: The complaint rate on the upper deck front cabin is 6.1 per thousand flight hours against a fleet figure of 0.9. We have carried two vendor investigations, both of which closed with no fault found on the units removed. Our own recording of the cabin distribution showed the feed dropping out of tolerance late in the cruise on four of the five aircraft instrumented. The pattern does not appear on the main deck, where the seat count per feeder is lower.
sections.expected_outcome: A permanent increase in the power available to the upper deck seat groups, sized for present-day passenger device loads, with the entertainment head end and the seat boxes both able to run at full load for a fourteen-hour sector without intervention by the crew, and no new despatch restriction.

type_data.business_justification: Premium cabin service failures at 6.1 per thousand flight hours, two closed vendor investigations with no fault found, and a compensation exposure the commercial department now tracks monthly.
